ANNOTATION_read_this_first.headline: A 3.0 m Route B sub-leg REACHED TARGET at 0.1484 m. Only 1 of 3 sub-legs ran, because of an operator-side payload omission, not a mower or splitter fault.

result.significance: First 3.0 m leg on record to land inside tolerance. n = 1, and it landed with 1.6 mm to spare -- this is a datapoint, NOT a demonstration that 3.0 m legs are reliable.

ANNOTATION_read_this_first.why_only_one_sub_leg_ran: The dispatch payload omitted `max_real_segments`, which defaulted to 1. The 2026-08-20 3.85 m run sent 4. Nothing about the splitter, the mower or the chain caused this -- the split was computed correctly (3 sub-legs of 2.999999 m) and the run simply stopped on `max_real_segments_reached` after the first. The collinear-junction question is therefore STILL untested end-to-end at 3.0 m.
ANNOTATION_read_this_first.the_scanned_path_was_not_the_driven_path: ⚠️ PROCESS GAP, worth fixing before the next run. The bearing scan and the dry run validated a leg from (7.3963, -0.3307). The operator then moved the mower to (6.229, -3.8881), and the dispatch script re-read the LIVE position and recomputed the endpoint from it along the same 303 deg heading. That sounds safe and is not: it silently drove a path the scan never covered. Re-deriving a target from live position INVALIDATES the scan that authorised it.

was_the_driven_path_actually_unsafe.verdict: NO -- and an earlier reading of this during the session overstated it.
was_the_driven_path_actually_unsafe.detail: Checked retroactively at 5 cm spacing: every sampled point on the full 9 m leg lies inside SOME mapped area, and minimum keep-out clearance was 5.01 m -- further from the trampoline zone than the scanned path was. What the stricter scan flags is that sub-leg 3 would have left the STARTING area (Backyard Right, 1343645155037768237) and entered the adjacent mapped area 3481535603736850863, whose polygons overlap in y. That is an area CROSSING, not an excursion onto unmapped ground.
was_the_driven_path_actually_unsafe.backend_behaved_correctly: `path_points_outside_known_area_geometry` tests each point against ANY known area polygon, so pt3 passing is the check working as designed, not a defect. The project scan is deliberately stricter: start-area only, plus a 0.60 m edge and 1.00 m keep-out margin.
was_the_driven_path_actually_unsafe.executed_sub_leg_clearance: Sub-leg 1, the only one driven, held 4.81 m minimum area-edge clearance and never approached any boundary.

what_is_still_owed: Re-run with `max_real_segments: 4` to test the 3.0 m chain end-to-end -- the actual Route B question.
Scan and dispatch must use the SAME path: freeze the scanned endpoint, or re-scan after any reposition.
BLE cadence degradation over run time (docs/evidence-ble-cadence-predictors-20260821.json) is untested here: this run lasted 63.6 s and only its first 3 m executed.
ANNOTATION_read_this_first.gate: Armed by the operator before the run; DISARMED and independently verified immediately after -- enabled false, real_motion_allowed false, blockers ['experimental_motion_disabled'].

safety_gates.name: stop_primitive_available
safety_gates.detail: Coordinator must expose async_stop_manual_motion().

safety_gates.name: ble_transport_required
safety_gates.detail: Real closed-loop motion requires the BLE transport for responsive telemetry; cloud/Wi-Fi lag is unsafe for guarded path execution. BLE must also report itself usable -- being selected for routing does not mean a command can be delivered.

safety_gates.name: ble_link_live
safety_gates.detail: Real motion requires a conservative BLE preflight -- a live client, an open dispatch gate, an empty command queue, and a recent outbound attempt. 'Usable' only means BLE is eligible for routing; it stays True while the command queue is gated and commands (including the mandatory stop that bounds a pulse) accumulate undelivered. The send path separately waits for confirmed queue start and GATT-write completion. See docs/pymammotion-ble-slot-leak-bug.md.

safety_gates.detail: Real pulse requires confirm_blades_off=true.

safety_gates.name: operator_confirmed_clear_area
safety_gates.detail: Real pulse requires confirm_clear_area=true.

safety_gates.name: mower_reports_blades_off
safety_gates.detail: Real pulse requires blade state off and cutter RPM zero/unknown.

safety_gates.name: mower_ready
safety_gates.detail: Real pulse requires the mower to be ready/paused, not mowing or charging.

safety_gates.name: not_docked_or_charging
safety_gates.detail: Real pulse requires the mower to be off the dock and not charging.

safety_gates.name: live_map_position_available
safety_gates.detail: Real pulse requires live map-local mower position.

safety_gates.name: position_area_inside
safety_gates.detail: Real pulse requires AREA_INSIDE, TURN_AREA_INSIDE, or CHANNEL_AREA_OVERLAP and a nonzero known zone hash.

safety_gates.name: map_position_nonzero
safety_gates.detail: Real pulse requires nonzero map-local x/y coordinates.

safety_gates.name: segment_too_long
safety_gates.detail: Segment length is capped at 6.1 m by authorization, not by a measured reach limit; the longest segment ever executed is 4.0 m.

safety_gates.name: linear_budget_insufficient_for_segment
safety_gates.detail: 22 linear pulses reach about 6.60 m at a stall-tolerant 0.3 m/pulse, short of this segment.
